question.problem:
$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}y+\frac{1}{3}, & \,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

The joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ for the continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is shown above. Given that 

$$
\text{E}[X]=\frac{2}{3},\,\text{E}[Y]=\frac{11}{18},\,\text{SD}[X]≈0.2582,\,\text{SD}[Y]≈0.2664,
$$

 
find the correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the correlation coefficient of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ is defined as

$$
\rho =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]},
$$

where

- $\text{Cov}[X,Y]$ is the covariance, and

- $\text{SD}[X]$ and $\text{SD}[Y]$ are the standard deviations of $X$ and $Y.$

First, by applying the rule of the lazy statistician, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}xy\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}xy\cdot (4{x}^{2}y+\frac{1}{3})\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}(4{x}^{3}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}xy)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[{x}^{4}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{6}{x}^{2}y]}_{x=0}^{x=1}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{2}+\frac{1}{6}y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}+\frac{1}{12}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{12} \\  & =\frac{5}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the covariance and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{5}{12}-(\frac{2}{3})(\frac{11}{18}) \\  & =\frac{1}{108}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correlation coefficient is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]} \\  & ≈\frac{(\frac{1}{108})}{(0.2582)\cdot (0.2664)} \\  & ≈0.13,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
